page.summary: Escort an active carry only when extra wiggle pressure or a short bodyblock can turn a marginal route into an escape; disengage if the Killer drops or turns on you.

verdict.recommendation: Assess carry distance and nearby hooks before entering the Killer's reach.
verdict.soloQ: Avoid speculative escorts without a readable hook route; the proximity cost is severe when the team cannot coordinate.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call one escort and the expected hook route so other players maintain objective pressure.
verdict.mainWeakness: Staying close to the carrying Killer exposes the escort to a hit or down, and the Killer can drop the teammate.

options.whyItsHere: While within 5 m of the Killer carrying another Survivor, it grants you 6/8/10% Haste and makes that Survivor wiggle 25% faster; only one Breakout effect applies to the carried Survivor.

opening: Before closing distance, judge whether the carry is close enough to a hook that escorting will only donate your health state.

rows.situation: A teammate is being carried along a marginal route and you can remain near without being immediately downed.
rows.action: Move within Breakout's 5 m range for the useful part of the carry, then peel away when the carried player escapes or the hook outcome is decided.
rows.why: The carried teammate wiggles faster only while you are close to the carrying Killer; proximity is the benefit and the risk.

rows.situation: One brief obstruction of the carry route could prevent the hook.
rows.action: Use your position only if the delay can change the outcome, and retain a route away after contact.
rows.why: A bodyblock with no escape payoff trades your health for nothing.

rows.situation: The Killer drops the Survivor, turns to hit you or reaches a hook your escort cannot contest.
rows.action: Leave the Killer's immediate range and reassess recovery or rescue instead of following a lost carry.
rows.why: The active-carry condition and escape pressure disappear once the carry ends.

abortWhen: The Killer drops the teammate or switches onto the escort.
The route is too short for extra wiggle pressure to matter or you cannot leave safely.

weaknesses: High exposure near the carrying Killer; a dropped Survivor or short route cancels the expected payoff.
commonMistakes: Entering close range before confirming the carry can be contested.
Continuing to escort after a drop or accepting a second down for no route gain.
